en: Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and accompanied by initial and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra*), there arises a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not accompanied by initial and sustained application, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … three.

Dependent on a state that is without-conflict and accompanied by initial and sustained application, there arises a state that is not without-conflict and not accompanied by initial and sustained application, by way of root condition … one.

Under root condition there are four; under object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two … pe … under result condition (*vipāka*) there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are four.

Dependent on a state that is a refuge (*saraṇa*) and consists of non-initial application with sustained application (*avitakkavicāramatta*), there arises a state that is not a refuge and does not consist of non-initial application with sustained application by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*) … [as above] … Under root condition there are four; under object condition there are two … [etc. … under result condition there is one … [etc. … under non-disappearance condition there are four.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and without initial application and sustained application (*avitakka-avicāra*), there arises a state that is not a refuge and does not consist of non-initial application and non-sustained application by way of root condition. Under root condition there is one … [etc. … under non-disappearance condition there is one.
